[P1] 在田野上萌生的《牛心》
在
田
野
上
萌
生
的
牛
心

[P2] 有一只小田鼠叫“沉闷”。
因为他住在一个潮湿的地洞里，
地洞又暗又小，没法蹦蹦跳跳，所以
小田鼠一直显得很沉闷。
那一天，麦子刚收割完，田野变得
光秃秃的。
小田鼠沉闷走出地洞，来到田野
上。
一只正在散步的小青蛙告诉小田
鼠，在收割后的田野上，常能捡到一
种叫“开心”的东西，捡到了就会很开心。什么样的东西叫“开心”呢？小

[P3] 田鼠不明白，他问青蛙，青蛙也讲不清楚。

尽管这样，小田鼠还是想去田野
走走。

他看见一只乌鸦从收割后的田野
上叼起一串麦穗，这是农民收割时
掉下的，乌鸦高兴得直拍翅膀。小田
鼠想：看来，乌鸦捡到他的“开心”了。

他看见一只小喜鹊在收割后的田野
上，发现一枚亮晶晶的小硬币，小喜鹊
围着硬币又唱又跳。小田鼠知道她捡
到“开心”了，因为谁都知道，小喜鹊喜
欢收集亮晶晶的东西。

小田鼠走啊走，他的心情很沉闷，
因为他总也捡不到让自己开心的东
西。

[P4] 突然，小田鼠在一片草丛中发现了一串东西，那是一串用小铁圈拴在一起的、叮当作响的东西。
“要是我没猜错的话，这是一串钥匙。”小田鼠听爸爸讲过，钥匙这个东西很重要，没有它就打不开家门，就回不了家。
“谁掉的钥匙呢？”小田鼠捡起钥匙。他问一只从他身边走过的小刺猬：“你掉钥匙了吗？”
小刺猬接过钥匙看了一下，说：“不，我住在泥洞里，我家的门整天开着，是不用钥匙的！”

[P5] 小田鼠看见田野边站着一个稻草人，他手里的那把扇子在不停地摇晃呢。
小田鼠跑过去说：“田野里的庄稼都收割了，你不用站在这儿了，快回家吧！这是你家的钥匙吗？”

稻草人看了一下小田鼠举起的钥匙，说：“不，我一年四季都在田野上，田野就是我的家。我的家没有门，也就不需要钥匙。”

[P6] “哦，我想起来了。”小田鼠自言自语道，“一定是那些帮着收割麦子的小孩子掉的。”
小田鼠想起他躲在地洞里的时候，曾听到孩子们的嬉闹声。他很想为那个掉了钥匙的孩子送去这串钥匙。
可是去村子里太危险了。
那些大人和孩子看见田鼠会把他打死的。再说，村子里的狗和猫也都是凶巴巴的。小田鼠想，还是把那串
钥匙扔掉吧。要不，他非但不能捡回“开心”，还可能碰上“危险”的。
小田鼠毫不犹豫地扔掉了这串钥匙。
可是，他只往前走了几步，就又转过身来。他说：“那小孩掉了钥匙多倒霉啊，他进不了家门。说不定他此刻口正渴、肚子正饿，很想回家啊。”
想到这里，小田鼠就捡起钥匙往

[P7] 村子里走去。
他沿着通往村子的小路急急忙忙地走着。
慢慢地，他看见村里的房舍了。
就在这时，他猛一抬头，看见前面的篱笆墙边，一只很凶狠的大黑猫正不好好意地瞅着他呢。小田鼠赶紧躲进路边的草丛里，这是一片很大的长着刺头儿的草，在这种草丛里走路真不好受。但为了躲开大黑猫，他不得不在草丛里穿行。他绕过篱笆墙，也就躲开了那只让他战战心惊的猫。

[P8] 小田鼠终于来到一片有着青砖红瓦的小农舍边。
他看见小农舍前有一个小男孩正在伤心地哭泣呢。小男孩的裤袋布都被翻到外面来了，他还在不住地挖自己上衣的口袋，可是他什么东西都没挖出来。
小农舍的门紧锁着。
小男孩哭得好伤心，他的眼里满是泪，鼻子抽抽搭搭的。
“准是这个糊涂蛋丢了钥匙！”
小田鼠想，“这个小男孩哭得真可怜……”
小田鼠站在离农舍不远的一片小灌木丛下，他扬起手臂一使劲，那串钥匙当啷一声落在了小男孩的脚边。

[P9] 小男孩吃了一惊。
当他低头一瞧，发现那串钥匙就在脚边的时候，脸上露出了笑容。就像太阳从乌云中探出脸来一样，他淌着泪的脸，一下子变得光亮起来。
小男孩笑得好开心。
不知为什么，小田鼠也一下子开心起来，原来常在心中作怪的沉闷，也一下子被赶走了。他真的好开心，开心得直想叫直想跳呢……

这时，小男孩捡起钥匙，打开了农舍的门。

然后，从农舍的门廊里，从农舍被打开的窗户里，飘出一阵阵很好听的歌声来。这歌声能让每个听到的人开心。

正当小田鼠也想高兴地唱歌时，

[P10] 突然从农舍后面蹿出一只凶猛的大黄狗来。大黄狗朝着小田鼠“汪汪”狂吠，小田鼠连忙退回灌木丛，钻进那片长着刺头儿的草丛里。大黄狗冲到草丛边，更大声地狂吠起来。
小田鼠顾不得身上被刺得火辣辣地痛，一口气跑回田野上。
田野上，庄稼被收割一空，显得光秃秃的。
小田鼠走在这片空地上，心里却很充实。他想起小男孩那清彻的笑脸，想起从小男孩的农舍飘出来的好听的歌声，心里就充满了快乐。小田鼠的身上还有一点点痛，由于大黄狗的狂吠和追赶，他的心还在“嗵嗵”地

[P11] 跳着，不过小田鼠真的很高兴。
小田鼠走在收割后的田野上，他
突然想起自己是来捡那种叫“开心”
的东西的——
“我捡到了！”小田鼠向空旷的
田野，大声地回答了自己。
full_text_en:
[P1] Born in the Fields: 'Cow's Heart'
In
the
fields
sprouts
the
Cow's
Heart

[P2] There was a little field mouse named "Chenmen".
Because he lived in a damp burrow,
the burrow was dark and small, so he couldn't hop around, and thus
the little field mouse always seemed very gloomy.
One day, after the wheat had been harvested, the field became
bald and bare.
The little field mouse Chenmen walked out of his burrow and arrived at the field.
A little frog who was taking a walk told the little field mouse,
"On the field after harvest, you often find something called 'happiness'. If you find it, you'll be very happy. What kind of thing is called 'happiness'?"

[P3] The field mouse didn't understand. He asked the frog, but the frog couldn't explain it either.

Still, the little field mouse wanted to go for a walk in the fields.

He saw a crow picking up a string of wheat ears from the harvested field. These had fallen during the harvest. The crow was so happy it flapped its wings. The field mouse thought: "Looks like the crow found its 'happiness.'"

He saw a little magpie in the harvested field, discovering a shiny little coin. The magpie danced and sang around the coin. The field mouse knew she had found her 'happiness,' because everyone knows magpies love collecting shiny things.

The field mouse walked and walked, but his mood remained gloomy, because he could never find anything that made him happy.

[P4] Suddenly, the little field mouse discovered a string of things in a patch of grass — a string of small iron rings tied together, jingling and clinking.
“If I’m not mistaken, this is a set of keys,” the little field mouse thought. He had heard his father say that keys were very important — without them, you couldn’t open your front door, and you couldn’t go home.
“Whose keys are these?” the little field mouse picked up the keys and asked a hedgehog passing by. “Did you drop them?”
The hedgehog took the keys and looked at them, then said, “No, I live in a mud hole. My door is always open — I don’t need keys!”

[P5] The little field mouse saw a scarecrow standing by the field, his fan swaying continuously.
The little field mouse ran over and said, “The crops in the field have all been harvested. You don’t need to stand here anymore. Go home! Is this your house key?”

The scarecrow looked at the key the little field mouse held up and said, “No, I’m on the field all year round. The field is my home. My home has no door, so I don’t need a key.”

[P6] "Oh, I remember now," the little field mouse murmured to himself, "It must have been dropped by one of the children who helped harvest the wheat." 

The little field mouse remembered how, when he was hiding in his burrow, he had heard the children's laughter. He really wanted to return the key to the child who had lost it. 

But going to the village was too dangerous. 

The grown-ups and children would kill him if they saw a field mouse. Besides, the dogs and cats in the village were all fierce. The little field mouse thought, maybe he should just throw the key away. 

Throwing the key away, he thought, would mean he couldn't find 'happiness' — and he might even run into 'danger'. 

Without hesitation, the little field mouse threw away the key. 

But then, after only a few steps forward, he turned back. He said, "That child must be so unlucky to have lost his key. He can't get home. He might be thirsty right now, or hungry, and just wants to go home." 

Thinking of this, the little field mouse picked up the key again and started walking toward the village.

[P7] He walked toward the village.
He hurried along the path leading to the village.
Slowly, he saw the houses in the village.
Just then, he suddenly looked up and saw a very fierce black cat by the fence, glaring at him. The little field mouse quickly hid in the grass by the roadside. It was a large patch of grass with prickly tips. Walking through this grass was really uncomfortable. But to avoid the big black cat, he had to weave through the grass. He went around the fence and thus avoided that cat that made him tremble with fear.

[P8] The little field mouse finally arrived at a small farmhouse with green bricks and red tiles.
He saw a little boy crying sadly in front of the farmhouse. The boy's pants pockets were turned inside out, and he kept digging into the pockets of his shirt, but couldn't find anything.
The farmhouse door was locked.
The little boy was crying bitterly, tears filling his eyes, his nose sniffling.
"It must be this clumsy fool who lost the key!"
The little field mouse thought, "This little boy is crying so pitifully..."
The little field mouse stood under a small bush not far from the farmhouse. He raised his arm and gave a strong push—the key clattered and fell at the boy's feet.

[P9] The little boy was startled.
When he looked down, he saw the bunch of keys right by his feet, and a smile appeared on his face. Just like the sun peeking out from behind the clouds, his tear-streaked face suddenly became bright.
The little boy was so happy.
For some reason, the little field mouse also felt instantly happy. The gloom that had been troubling him was suddenly gone. He was truly happy, so happy he wanted to shout and jump!

At that moment, the little boy picked up the keys and opened the door of the farmhouse.

Then, from the porch of the farmhouse, from the windows that had been opened, came a series of beautiful songs. These songs could make everyone who heard them happy.

Just as the little field mouse was about to sing happily,

[P10] Suddenly, a fierce yellow dog burst out from behind the farmhouse. The yellow dog barked wildly at the little field mouse, "Woof woof!" The little field mouse hurriedly retreated into the shrubs and squeezed into the patch of grass with prickly tips. The yellow dog rushed to the edge of the grass, barking even louder.
The little field mouse didn't care about the stinging pain on his body and ran back to the field in one breath.
On the field, the crops had been harvested, leaving it bare and bare.
The little field mouse walked on this empty land, but his heart felt full. He remembered the boy's clear smile, and the pleasant songs drifting from the boy's farmhouse, filling his heart with joy. The little field mouse still felt a little pain on his body, and due to the yellow dog's wild barking and chasing, his heart was still "thumping".

[P11] Jumping, but the little field mouse was really happy.
The little field mouse walked across the harvested field, and suddenly remembered that he had come to pick up something called "happiness"—
"I found it!" the little field mouse shouted loudly to the open field, answering himself.
full_summary_zh:
[P1] 本页为绘本标题页，以竖排黄色字体展示书名《在田野上萌生的〈牛心〉》，背景为粉红色纹理纸张。
[P2] 本页介绍了主角小田鼠“沉闷”因居住环境潮湿狭小而性格忧郁，收割后的田野变得光秃秃，他走出地洞，遇到一只正在散步的小青蛙，青蛙告诉他田野上能捡到叫“开心”的东西，引发他对“开心”的好奇。
[P3] 小田鼠在收割后的田野上，看到乌鸦捡到麦穗、喜鹊捡到硬币，都认为它们找到了‘开心’，但自己却始终找不到让自己开心的东西，心情依然沉闷。
[P4] 小田鼠在草丛中发现一串钥匙，以为是能带来‘开心’的东西，便捡起询问路过的小刺猬，但小刺猬表示自己住泥洞，门整天开着，不需要钥匙，小田鼠的期待再次落空。
[P5] 小田鼠在田野边发现一个稻草人，以为他需要钥匙回家，便将自己捡到的钥匙递给他，但稻草人解释自己一年四季都在田野上，田野就是家，不需要钥匙。
[P6] 小田鼠在田野上捡到一串钥匙，起初想归还给失主，但因担心去村子里太危险而决定扔掉。然而，想到失主可能口渴、饥饿、想回家，他最终又捡起钥匙，准备送还。
[P7] 小田鼠走向村子，途中发现一只凶狠的大黑猫正盯着他，他赶紧躲进路边长满刺的草丛中，绕过篱笆墙以避开黑猫。
[P8] 小田鼠来到农舍边，看到一个男孩因丢了钥匙而伤心哭泣，便将自己捡到的钥匙送还给他。
[P9] 小男孩找到钥匙后开心地打开了农舍的门，歌声随之飘出，小田鼠也因这份喜悦而心情大好，正想唱歌时，故事戛然而止。
[P10] 小田鼠在躲避大黄狗后跑回田野，虽然身上被刺痛，但想起小男孩的笑脸和歌声，内心感到充实和快乐，尽管身体仍有疼痛，心仍在跳动。
[P11] 小田鼠在收割后的田野上，想起自己捡到的钥匙其实是“开心”的东西，于是兴奋地向田野宣告自己找到了它。
